summary: The first_proof_2 dataset spans 10 open research-level problems, with proof activity heavily concentrated on q10 (8 open issues, including core preconditioner and MTTKRP/RHS-formation subtasks) and rm-02193 (4 open issues decomposing a BGH fixed-endpoint and merging algorithm). Most problems (q1–q5, q7–q10) have accumulated 100 proof issues each, indicating broad engagement, while q6 stands out with only 9 — either near-complete or under-attempted. Several entries (rm-01413, rm-01541, rm-13126, q10's '__probe__delete__') are probe/void artifacts that should be cleaned up to keep the tracker honest.
problems: q10 carries the most open work (8 issues): preconditioner choice (G2 CORE), RHS/MTTKRP B=TZ formation (G4), plus a stray '__probe__delete__' probe issue mixed into real tasks.

rm-02193 has 4 open issues breaking one proof into component subroutines (BGH fixed-endpoint, merging algorithm) plus a minor 'unique topological order' concern — a well-decomposed, near-tractable proof.
Every prob-01 through prob-10 has exactly 1 open 'Proof:' issue and 0 resolved, so no benchmark problem has a confirmed solution yet.
q6 has only 9 proof issues versus 100 for its peers, signaling either it is close to closure or it is being neglected and needs triage.
Probe/void issues pollute the tracker: rm-01413 ([VOID] created in error), rm-01541 (probe2 delete me), rm-13126 (PROBE/NS-PROBE), and q10's '__probe__delete__' should be removed.
Resolution rate is effectively zero — only test/probe issues (rm-01413, rm-01541) are marked resolved, while all substantive proof issues remain open.
highlights: q10 shows the strongest traction with concrete, well-scoped engineering subtasks (preconditioner, MTTKRP RHS), making incremental progress measurable.
rm-02193's decomposition into named component subroutines suggests an active solver close to assembling a full proof.
Broad coverage: 8 of 10 problems have reached the 100-issue activity ceiling, so attention is distributed rather than stalled on one problem.
The dataset's issue structure is clean enough to identify probe/void noise quickly and separate it from genuine proof work.

suggested_todos.title: Push q10 to closure by resolving the G2 preconditioner-choice and G4 RHS/MTTKRP formation issues, the two core blockers
Assemble rm-02193's component subroutines (BGH fixed-endpoint + merging algorithm) into a single end-to-end proof and resolve the topological-order minor
Triage q6 to determine whether its low issue count (9) means near-completion or neglect, and rebalance effort accordingly
Delete probe/void issues (rm-01413, rm-01541, rm-13126, q10 '__probe__delete__') to de-noise the tracker
Schedule a first resolution milestone for any prob-01..prob-10 issue, since none of the 10 benchmark problems has a single resolved proof yet
